correctness.rationale: Counting measure on Omega=N is valid for continuous definitions, each one-point local frame of C has exact positive bound, and all weave labels are identical. In direction (g to vector), Lambda_n f=f_n is Parseval while F_n(*)=1/n produces vectors e_n/n with squared analysis norm sum |f_n|^2/n^2, refuted by test f=e_N. In reverse, Lambda_n f=f_n/n is not a g-frame and F_n(*)=n yields standard ONB vectors e_n, hence woven Parseval. No unbounded operator is asserted (each Lambda_n bounded). For uniform local inequalities a||Lambda_n f||²<=E_local<=b||Lambda_n f||², integrate over each partition to obtain aE_g<=E_vec<=bE_g; outer bounds C,D transfer to aC,bD and vector bounds to C/b,D/a. Both missing conditions are therefore material to the intended universal theorem. The 2020 original Theorem 2.7 indexed author full-text extract and the 2023 full PDF Theorem 0.12 have identical inf/sup passages without uniform bounds.

originality.rationale: The full published 2020 theorem (Theorem 2.7, pp.29-30) was compared term-by-term with its proof: locally indexed A_{F_{omega i}}, B_{F_{omega i}} are allowed, yet inf A and sup B are treated as strictly positive/finite without hypotheses. The 2023 extension Theorem 0.12 repeats this dependence rather than supplying a counterexample/correction. A distinct published local dual-frame pathology uses related diagonal sequences, but addresses a different alternate-duality assertion and does not correct this weaving equivalence. Bounded searches for theorem number, DOI, frame bound inf/sup, counterexamples and erratum found no prior correction resolving precisely both directions. Originality is best of knowledge, not a claim that diagonal weighting is new.
residual_risks: The 2020 author-hosted original PDF itself was not downloaded owing to web access; however the complete Theorem 2.7 statement and the proof passages needed for the claim were materially read from an indexed rendering.
An unindexed erratum or thesis correction could independently give the examples and uniform repair.
The corrected constants are sufficient for arbitrary frames; specially compensating nonuniform cases may also preserve equivalence.

value.rationale: The claim repairs an actual published necessary-and-sufficient theorem and an independent published extension, with two direction-specific examples and transferred constants. This is a substantive scope/correctness defect in a structural frame equivalence, not merely a trivial renaming of frame normalization.

final_claim: Theorem 2.7 of Alizadeh-Sadri (2020) cannot assert equivalence of continuous g-weaving of operator fields and weaving of vectors induced through merely pointwise local frames; two countably indexed one-dimensional counterexamples separately force global lower and upper local-frame control. Uniform constants 0<a<=b<infinity provide the corrected quantitative equivalence via a E_g(f)<=E_vec(f)<=b E_g(f) for every weave.
limitations: Counterexamples use discrete counting measure, legitimate subcase of continuous theory; no exotic inner measurability is needed.
The result does not characterize every nonglobal-coercive local field that by coincidence yields equivalent weaving.
